recognize_zh: 低倍血片中大量小而緻密、無中央淡染區的球形紅血球（spherocytes），夾雜偏藍的多染性紅血球與數個有核紅血球，並可見紅血球小團塊聚集，符合免疫性血管外溶血。
features: Numerous spherocytes: small, dense, round red cells lacking central pallor
Scattered nucleated red blood cells with small dense pyknotic nuclei
Small red cell aggregates/clumps in the thin area of the film
Occasional neutrophils and markedly reduced platelets
No schistocytes identified at this magnification
describe_en: Low-power view of the peripheral blood smear shows marked anisocytosis with a prominent population of spherocytes and conspicuous polychromasia. Several circulating nucleated red blood cells are present, along with small red cell aggregates. Scattered neutrophils are seen and platelets are markedly decreased; no significant schistocytes are identified at this power. In the setting of a recent RhD-incompatible transfusion and a positive direct antiglobulin test, findings are consistent with extravascular immune hemolysis due to a delayed hemolytic transfusion reaction.

ddx.vs: HS shows spherocytes with a negative DAT, family history, and no nucleated RBC surge or red cell clumping tied to recent transfusion, whereas DHTR is DAT-positive with a new alloantibody.

Morphology is identical (spherocytes, polychromasia); separation relies on eluate specificity—an alloantibody against transfused antigen (e.g. anti-D) in DHTR versus a panreactive autoantibody in WAIHA.
Cold agglutinins produce large irregular RBC agglutinates that disperse on warming with DAT positive for C3 only, rather than predominant spherocytes with IgG-mediated extravascular hemolysis.
TTP also causes severe thrombocytopenia but shows schistocytes with a negative DAT, whereas this film is dominated by spherocytes without evident fragments.
